look_here_first: LOOK FIRST at a mature anthocarp: it should be glabrous, with relatively acute five ribs and a truncate to low-conic apex. Then inspect the loose branching flower clusters and whether leaves are mostly on the lower part of an often annual plant.

project_inclusion.learner_admission_basis: Calvin-approved Nyctaginaceae source-pool genus roadmap and completed Boerhavia scientific review in content/taxa/Nyctaginaceae/family.json
project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO records Texas as native at state scale; no project target-zone three-county PASS was established in completed review. Photo geography is not county occurrence evidence.

best_field_traits: Small white to pinkish flowers in diffuse branching clusters; single petaloid perianth whorl.
Mature anthocarps about 2.7–4 mm, glabrous, with acute ribs and truncate/low-conic apex.
Usually annual habit; leaves concentrated mostly in the lower half of the plant. Leaf distribution alone is not decisive.

confused_with: Boerhavia triquetra var. intermedia (historical B. intermedia)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Unlike B. coccinea, B. erecta lacks densely stalked-glandular fruit hairs. Unlike B. linearifolia, its fruit ribs are sharp/acute rather than broadly rounded with smooth intervening grooves. Fruits overlap in length with the B. intermedia complex; compare mature fruit apex and irregular versus more precise terminal umbels.
